agenda: The situation between Iraq and Kuwait
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The United Kingdom's primary objective is to maintain an institutionalized UN mechanism and regular Security Council reporting on missing Kuwaiti persons and archives following the drawdown of UNAMI, while reaffirming border commitments under resolution 833 (1993). Difficult negotiations are expected with Iraq-friendly members (such as Algeria and Russia) regarding the establishment of a post-UNAMI High-Level Coordinator, which Baghdad may perceive as prolonging Chapter VII-related scrutiny, and with respect to maritime demarcation language given sensitive domestic political and judicial developments in Iraq concerning the Khor Abdullah agreement.

messages.Algeria: Algeria attaches great importance to the fraternal relations between Iraq and Kuwait and supports efforts to bring closure to the deeply humanitarian issues of missing persons and archives. As UNAMI transitions toward closure pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), any post-UNAMI mechanism must be established in close consultation and alignment with both Baghdad and Kuwait City, respecting the sovereignty of Iraq and keeping the footprint streamlined and focused. Furthermore, outstanding bilateral matters, including maritime demarcation, should be advanced through voluntary, constructive bilateral dialogue founded on mutual consent.
messages.China: China supports the continuous improvement of bilateral relations between Iraq and Kuwait and appreciates the humanitarian importance of resolving the issue of missing persons and property. Any post-UNAMI United Nations follow-up mechanism must fully respect the sovereignty of Iraq, take into account the views and consent of both Iraq and Kuwait, and avoid imposing unnecessary oversight or bureaucratic expansion. We encourage the penholder to ensure that the mechanism remains lean, efficient, and strictly supportive of the parties' cooperative efforts.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports this draft resolution and thanks the United Kingdom for its leadership in ensuring a seamless transition following UNAMI's drawdown. We welcome the focus on international law, peaceful settlement of disputes in line with UNCLOS, and the urgent humanitarian file of missing persons and return of property. We propose a minor addition in preambular paragraph 7 to underline a family-centred approach in line with the Council's established practice on missing persons in armed conflict.
messages.France: France commends the United Kingdom for circulating this balanced and timely draft resolution, which addresses the crucial humanitarian file of missing Kuwaiti persons and property ahead of UNAMI's drawdown. As an active member of the Tripartite Commission, France attaches the highest importance to resolving these issues and upholding resolution 833 (1993) and international law. Ensuring that the new follow-up mechanism is established in close consultation with both Baghdad and Kuwait will be essential for its operational effectiveness and broad Council consensus.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom. We particularly welcome the explicit reference to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) regarding maritime demarcation, the reaffirmation of the inviolability of international borders pursuant to resolution 833 (1993), and the priority given to the purely humanitarian imperative of accounting for missing persons. We also support the establishment of a dedicated United Nations follow-up mechanism and High-Level Coordinator to ensure seamless continuity as UNAMI transitions.
messages.Guyana: Guyana fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the United Kingdom. We particularly welcome the reaffirmation of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the inviolability of the internationally demarcated border under resolution 833 (1993), as well as the call for maritime boundary delimitation in accordance with UNCLOS. We also underline the critical humanitarian imperative of resolving the files of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing property, and we support the establishment of a dedicated United Nations follow-up mechanism upon UNAMI's drawdown.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan shares deep, fraternal ties with both Iraq and Kuwait and fully supports efforts to bring closure to the families of missing persons and resolve outstanding humanitarian files. In light of the planned transition of UNAMI, we believe any follow-up mechanism must be focused, cost-effective, and established in close consultation and partnership with both Governments. We also encourage text that promotes consensual bilateral dialogue on maritime issues in a spirit of mutual respect and good neighbourliness.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution presented by the United Kingdom. We welcome the emphasis on resolving the lingering humanitarian issues regarding missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and the return of Kuwaiti property, as well as the reaffirmation of international law, the UN Charter, and the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea for the peaceful settlement of maritime boundaries. Establishing a dedicated follow-up mechanism and High-Level Coordinator ensures continuity following UNAMI's transition and fosters sustained regional stability and good neighbourly relations.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution prepared by the United Kingdom. Given our own historical experience, we place paramount importance on the humanitarian imperative of bringing closure to the families of missing persons and securing the return of national property and archives. We particularly welcome the timely establishment of a dedicated follow-up mechanism and High-Level Coordinator to ensure continuity following UNAMI's transition, as well as the text's robust reaffirmation of international law, UNCLOS, and good-neighbourly relations between Iraq and Kuwait.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the humanitarian objective of resolving the issues of missing Kuwaiti persons and property, which our country has historically contributed to under resolution 1284 (1999). However, any follow-up mechanism established after UNAMI's drawdown must fully respect Iraqi sovereignty and proceed strictly with Baghdad's consent and ownership, without creating redundant or costly bureaucratic structures. Furthermore, bilateral matters such as maritime demarcation beyond Pillar 162 must remain strictly between the two sovereign neighbors without outside prescription.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft resolution and welcomes the penholder's efforts to ensure seamless continuity on the crucial humanitarian issue of missing persons and Kuwaiti property ahead of UNAMI's drawdown. We believe explicitly anchoring the establishment of the follow-up mechanism in close consultation with both Iraq and Kuwait will foster national ownership and sustained bilateral cooperation. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and all Council members towards a consensus text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia expresses strong support for the UK draft resolution, which provides a necessary and practical framework to ensure United Nations engagement on missing persons and Kuwaiti property continues uninterrupted following UNAMI's drawdown. We welcome the emphasis on international law, resolution 833 (1993), and the humanitarian role of the ICRC and Tripartite Commission. We suggest a minor refinement to preambular paragraph 7 to anchor this humanitarian file in international humanitarian law and the right of families to know the fate of their loved ones.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the draft resolution submitted by the United Kingdom and expresses its full support for its adoption. As a fellow Arab League member with close, fraternal ties to both Iraq and Kuwait, Somalia attaches the highest importance to resolving the humanitarian file of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals, as well as the return of Kuwaiti national archives and property. We believe that establishing a dedicated United Nations follow-up mechanism and appointing a High-Level Coordinator upon the drawdown of UNAMI is an appropriate, balanced, and necessary step to maintain progress and bring closure to the families.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this timely draft resolution to ensure uninterrupted UN oversight and support on the repatriation of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and the return of Kuwaiti property as UNAMI draws down. Resolving these longstanding humanitarian files remains a vital priority for regional stability and closure for the families. We propose technical adjustments to align the maritime reference with standard language on international law of the sea and to ensure budgetary prudence.

before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
President,

The United Kingdom is pleased to present this draft resolution to the Council today.

More than thirty years after the Gulf War, the pain endured by the families of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains an open wound. It is a profound humanitarian imperative that we provide answers and closure to these families without further delay, and ensure the full return of Kuwait’s national property, including its National Archives.

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq prepares for its transition and drawdown pursuant to resolution 2732, the international community cannot allow these vital humanitarian files to be left behind. The draft resolution before us establishes a lean, dedicated, and effective follow-up mechanism under the authority of the Secretary-General, anchored by a High-Level Coordinator, to ensure continuous international support, coordination, and reporting in close partnership with the Governments of Iraq and Kuwait, the Tripartite Commission, and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

We commend both Iraq and Kuwait for their enduring commitment, cooperation, and constructive engagement in addressing these legacy issues. This resolution reinforces that partnership and upholds the Council’s enduring responsibility to support full reconciliation and regional stability.

We thank all Council members for their constructive engagement during negotiations, and we urge all delegations to vote in favour of this important humanitarian resolution. Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Council. 

We welcome the adoption of this text, which addresses a matter of profound humanitarian significance for the brotherly nations of Kuwait and Iraq, as well as for the wider region. More than three decades after the tragic events of 1990, the plight of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains a deeply painful issue. Providing closure and long-awaited answers to the families who have endured decades of agonizing uncertainty is an imperative that transcends politics. In this regard, we reaffirm the fundamental right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of their missing loved ones, in accordance with international humanitarian law and resolution 2474.

Algeria commends the Government of Iraq for its continued dedication, genuine political will, and tangible efforts to fulfill its obligations, despite the complex security and logistical challenges it faces. We equally commend the Government of Kuwait for its steadfast cooperation, constructive engagement, and generous support to the joint efforts undertaken within the Tripartite mechanism, expertly chaired by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). 

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI) prepares for its drawdown and closure pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is vital that the momentum achieved on these crucial humanitarian files—both regarding missing persons and the return of Kuwaiti property, including the National Archives—is not lost. We welcome that the mechanism established today by the Council is streamlined, focused, and, above all, anchored in the consent and close cooperation of both sovereign Governments.

Algeria remains deeply committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of both Iraq and Kuwait. We are heartened by the steady consolidation of their bilateral relations and encourage both brotherly countries to continue building on this constructive dialogue, in the noble spirit of good neighbourliness and Arab brotherhood, to resolve all remaining outstanding matters.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

More than thirty years after the Gulf War, resolving the issues of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and the return of Kuwaiti property, including the National Archives, remains an important humanitarian task. Bringing closure to the families of the missing and ensuring the return of property are crucial steps towards fostering lasting reconciliation, healing historical wounds, and promoting regional peace and stability.

China commends the sustained commitment and active efforts demonstrated by the Government of Iraq in fulfilling its relevant obligations under Security Council resolutions, despite facing numerous domestic challenges. We also express our appreciation for the constructive engagement and goodwill shown by the Government of Kuwait, as well as the important role played by the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Tripartite mechanism. The steady improvement in bilateral relations between Iraq and Kuwait in recent years is encouraging, demonstrating that dialogue, mutual respect, and consultation are the only viable path to resolving complex historical issues.

With the planned drawdown and closure of the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is both necessary and appropriate for the United Nations to maintain focused attention on these outstanding humanitarian files. China supports the establishment of a streamlined, dedicated, and cost-effective follow-up mechanism under the Secretary-General, working with the consent of and in close consultation with the Governments of Iraq and Kuwait. We hope that the newly appointed High-Level Coordinator will perform their duties in close coordination with all relevant parties, fully respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, and giving full play to existing bilateral and multilateral channels.

China has consistently advocated for peaceful coexistence and good-neighbourliness among countries in the region. We encourage Iraq and Kuwait to continue strengthening dialogue, properly handling remaining issues, and deepening mutually beneficial cooperation. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue supporting Iraq and Kuwait in building a future of enduring peace, stability, and shared development.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France welcomed and voted in favour of the resolution just adopted unanimously by the Security Council.

More than thirty years after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait, the question of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals, as well as the return of Kuwaiti property, including the National Archives, remains first and foremost a profound humanitarian imperative. For the families who continue to grieve and await answers about the fate of their loved ones, time has not lessened the pain. We owe them clarity, dignity, and closure.

As an active member of the Tripartite Commission, France pays tribute to the tireless and indispensable work carried out by the International Committee of the Red Cross in chairing this mechanism. We commend the constructive engagement and cooperation between the Governments of Iraq and Kuwait. While notable progress has been made over the years, significant challenges remain, particularly in locating remaining burial sites and recovering the National Archives. We encourage the Iraqi authorities to pursue their efforts with determination and to explore all available avenues and technological tools to achieve tangible results.

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq prepares its transition and drawdown pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it was essential that the Council ensure continuity and maintain a dedicated United Nations mechanism to support these humanitarian efforts. France welcomes the establishment of the post of High-Level Coordinator under the authority of the Secretary-General, which will ensure that this vital work proceeds seamlessly and in close coordination with both Governments and the Tripartite Commission.

Finally, France reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both Iraq and Kuwait, and to the inviolability of their international boundary, in accordance with international law and relevant Security Council resolutions, notably resolution 833 (1993). We encourage both States to continue building on their positive bilateral momentum in a spirit of good-neighbourliness and dialogue.

Thank you.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece welcomed the opportunity to vote in favour of the resolution just adopted and thanks the United Kingdom for its constructive role as penholder in facilitating this text.

More than thirty years after the events of 1990 and 1991, the unresolved fate of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains a matter of profound humanitarian concern. For Greece, the plight of missing persons and the enduring suffering of their families is an issue of the utmost sensitivity and priority. Families have an inalienable right to know the fate and whereabouts of their loved ones, in full accordance with international humanitarian law and Security Council resolution 2474 (2019). We commend the ongoing work of the Tripartite Commission and the International Committee of the Red Cross, as well as the cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, while urging continued and intensified efforts to locate and identify all remaining mortal remains, as well as the return of Kuwait's National Archives and property.

As UNAMI prepares for its drawdown pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is vital that the United Nations maintains a dedicated, effective mechanism to support these outstanding humanitarian files. We therefore welcome the decision to establish a follow-up mechanism and to appoint a High-Level Coordinator under the Secretary-General to ensure that this crucial work continues without interruption.

Finally, Greece underscores the paramount importance of full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both Iraq and Kuwait, and the inviolability of their international boundary as demarcated pursuant to resolution 833 (1993). We encourage both nations to continue their constructive dialogue in a spirit of good neighbourliness to resolve all outstanding bilateral issues, including the demarcation of their maritime boundary in strict adherence to international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

Thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Security Council. 

Pakistan enjoys deep-rooted, fraternal relations with both Kuwait and Iraq, based on shared faith, mutual respect, and historic ties. Our position on this agenda item has consistently been guided by our enduring commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of both brotherly nations, as well as the imperative of promoting peace, stability, and good-neighbourliness in the region.

More than three decades after the tragic events of the Gulf War, the pain of the families of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains a pressing humanitarian concern. Bringing closure to these families is a moral and humanitarian imperative that transcends politics. We commend the Government of Kuwait for its steadfast commitment, cooperation, and patience in pursuing these files. At the same time, we express our appreciation for the Government of Iraq’s continued cooperation and efforts to fulfill its obligations under relevant Council resolutions, despite the profound security and political challenges it has confronted over the years.

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI) prepares for its transition and drawdown pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is vital that the momentum on these outstanding humanitarian files is sustained. Pakistan supports the establishment of a streamlined, dedicated follow-up mechanism under the authority of the Secretary-General, working in full consultation and cooperation with both Iraq and Kuwait, the Tripartite Commission, and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

We welcome the continued improvement in bilateral relations between Baghdad and Kuwait City. We encourage both Governments to continue building upon this spirit of dialogue, mutual trust, and good-neighbourliness to resolve all remaining issues, including maritime boundary demarcation, in accordance with international law and the principles of the UN Charter.

Pakistan remains committed to supporting all constructive efforts that contribute to the lasting peace, security, and prosperity of the fraternal peoples of Iraq and Kuwait, and the wider region.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and welcomes its unanimous adoption by the Security Council today. We express our appreciation to the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its constructive leadership and dedicated efforts throughout the consultations.

More than three decades have passed since the end of the Gulf War, yet the anguish and uncertainty endured by the families of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remain an open wound. The search for the missing is, above all, a profound humanitarian imperative. In line with Council resolution 2474 (2019), my delegation reaffirms the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of their loved ones, and we stress the vital need to bring long-awaited answers and closure to these families without further delay.

In this regard, we commend the Governments of both Iraq and Kuwait for their enduring cooperation and dialogue, and we express our deep gratitude to the International Committee of the Red Cross for its steadfast leadership of the Tripartite Commission mechanism. We also welcome the ongoing efforts to locate and identify human remains, as well as the efforts to recover the missing Kuwaiti National Archives and property, while calling for these endeavours to be accelerated.

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI) prepares for its transition and drawdown pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is imperative that the momentum on these outstanding humanitarian files is neither lost nor interrupted. We therefore welcome the Council’s decision today to establish a streamlined, dedicated United Nations follow-up mechanism under the authority of the Secretary-General, and we look forward to the early appointment of the High-Level Coordinator to lead this important work in close consultation with the parties concerned.

Finally, the Republic of Korea welcomes the continued positive trajectory of bilateral relations between Iraq and Kuwait. We encourage both neighbours to maintain this constructive spirit of cooperation and dialogue to resolve all remaining issues, including maritime boundary demarcation, in full accordance with international law, the UN Charter, and relevant Security Council resolutions. 

My delegation reaffirms its steadfast commitment to supporting peace, stability, and prosperity in the region, and we stand ready to continue engaging constructively with both Iraq and Kuwait as valued partners.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian):

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by the United Kingdom. 

Our position of principle is based on the necessity of fully resolving all outstanding issues between Iraq and Kuwait resulting from the tragic events of more than three decades ago, primarily the purely humanitarian issue of clarifying the fate of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals, as well as the return of Kuwaiti property and the National Archives. We deeply sympathize with the families who have waited so many years to learn the fate of their loved ones.

Russia consistently supports the normalization and strengthening of good-neighbourly relations between Baghdad and Kuwait City, based on the principles of mutual respect, sovereignty, and territorial integrity. We commend the constructive bilateral dialogue between the two fraternal States and the consistent commitment demonstrated by the Government of Iraq to fulfilling its international obligations, despite the complex security and socio-economic challenges it continues to face. We also pay tribute to the indispensable role played by the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Tripartite mechanism.

With the planned drawdown and closure of the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq in accordance with resolution 2732 (2024) and the expressed wishes of the Iraqi authorities, it was essential to ensure that these humanitarian matters are not neglected. At the same time, it is of paramount importance that the follow-up mechanism established today operate in close coordination with and with the full consent of both Baghdad and Kuwait City, adhere strictly to its humanitarian mandate, maintain a lean administrative structure, and not impose unnecessary bureaucratic or political burdens.

We trust that the appointment of a High-Level Coordinator will impart additional momentum to the search and repatriation efforts, bringing closure to these long-standing humanitarian files and further fostering stability and trust in the region.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Slovenia welcomed the opportunity to vote in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we thank the United Kingdom for its constructive leadership as penholder throughout the negotiations.

More than three decades after the Gulf War, the issue of missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains a deeply painful humanitarian file. For Slovenia, addressing the plight of missing persons and upholding the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of their loved ones—in line with international humanitarian law and resolution 2474 (2019)—is a moral imperative and an indispensable component of post-conflict healing and reconciliation. 

With the planned drawdown and transition of UNAMI pursuant to resolution 2732 (2024), it is essential that the international community maintain uninterrupted engagement on these humanitarian obligations. We therefore strongly support the establishment of the dedicated United Nations follow-up mechanism and the appointment of a High-Level Coordinator to ensure continuity and focus in close cooperation with both Governments.

We commend the ongoing constructive dialogue and growing partnership between Iraq and Kuwait. We also express our sincere appreciation for the tireless work of the Tripartite Commission and the International Committee of the Red Cross. We urge further accelerated efforts to locate, excavate, and identify remaining burial sites, as well as to achieve meaningful progress on the return of Kuwait’s National Archives and missing property.

Finally, Slovenia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the principles of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both Iraq and Kuwait, including the inviolability of their demarcated border. 

I thank you.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution, and we thank the United Kingdom for its diligent leadership and penholdership on this important text.

More than thirty years after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait, the search for missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals remains a profound humanitarian imperative. Hundreds of families continue to endure the anguish of not knowing the fate of their loved ones. They deserve answers, and they deserve closure without further delay. Similarly, the return of Kuwait’s national archives and stolen property is essential to restoring Kuwait’s cultural and national heritage.

As the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq prepares for its drawdown and transition in accordance with resolution 2732, the international community has a duty to ensure that these outstanding humanitarian files are not forgotten. Today’s resolution fulfills that duty by establishing a dedicated, streamlined follow-up mechanism under the authority of the Secretary-General and calling for the appointment of a High-Level Coordinator. This will maintain focus, momentum, and accountability on these vital issues.

The United States commends the Governments of Kuwait and Iraq for their constructive bilateral engagement and their enduring commitment to working together in a spirit of good neighbourliness. We also express our deep gratitude to the International Committee of the Red Cross for its tireless dedication in chairing the Tripartite Commission and its Technical Sub-Committee, of which the United States is a proud and active member.

We urge the Government of Iraq to accelerate its efforts to locate and identify remaining burial sites and to pursue all available leads regarding the missing Kuwaiti archives. At the same time, we reaffirm our steadfast support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of both Iraq and Kuwait, and underline the importance of respecting the international boundary established pursuant to Security Council resolution 833.

Today’s unanimous vote demonstrates the Council’s enduring unity and commitment to supporting both Iraq and Kuwait as they build a peaceful, cooperative, and prosperous future together.

Thank you, Mr. President.
